title: Sebastiano Foscarini, Venetian ambassador in France, to the Doge, Paris 11 September 1680, despatch no. 117 (ASVe Busta 30 f. 4, DECODE R1871)

steps.what: Fetched R1871-R1873 images with the DECODE cookie and viewed them; identified Foscarini (Paris 11 Sep 1680, despatch no. 117) from the signature and docket.
Followed Tomokiyo's R1872 note to Bonavoglia's page (live site HTTP 500); the Wayback copy lists the Foscarini 1680-09-11 despatch as deciphered but shows only the default (Mocenigo) decipherment.
Transcribed R1871's cipher page (23 lines, 1,839 digits) from deskewed strips with two agents.
Tested pair and self-delimiting ([1-4]*[5-0], [1-5]*[6-0]) segmentations; homophonic annealing gave no Italian.
Found rare digits 0/7/8/9 fixed mod 3 within lines: 3-digit groups; DP segmentation to 612 groups, 211 distinct.
Monotone (ordered syllabary) annealer, 12 seeds, clean Italian 4-gram; synthetic ordered control recovered in part, real text not.
Sukhotin vowel test: vowel-like and consonant-like codes interleave, so the table is not alphabetical.
Free letter-per-code and letter/syllable annealers, 14 seeds: seed-dependent overfit gibberish.
Searched for the key and Bonavoglia's Foscarini page: DECODE Venetian keys R1788-R1790 (16th c., no match); crittologia storia page 404/refused, not archived.

Split from the former combined target r1871 (catalogue 264) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1873 (Mocenigo 1558, read from Bonavoglia's decipherment) moved to its own entry r1873; this entry keeps R1871 only, whose outcome is not solved. Earlier steps are kept as recorded.

outcome.method_basis: R1871 was transcribed (1,839 digits, 612 groups) and attacked ciphertext-only with several annealers without result; Bonavoglia's decipherment of it is listed but offline and was never seen, and no key is reachable.
outcome.notes: Attempted, not deciphered: 3-digit homophonic/syllabic nomenclator, one page too short to solve blind; key and Bonavoglia's decipherment unreachable.

credits.note: "Decifra dispacci veneziani" (crittologia.eu) lists this despatch (1680-09-11) as deciphered and describes Foscarini's cipher; the decipherment itself could not be retrieved
note on DECODE R1872 pointing to Bonavoglia's decipherments

gaps.detail: key not available anywhere reachable; Bonavoglia's decipherment offline; one page too short for a blind solution of a ~300-code homophonic table

prior.where: Paolo Bonavoglia lists the despatch as deciphered (crittologia.eu venezia_nomenclatore.html list; storia/SebFoscarini_Parigi16800911.html), but the decipherment is offline and was never seen

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
